text: dsh-codex-hooks 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的生命周期钩子管理插件。它接入 agent、工具调用、审批和会话结束等事件，从用户配置、插件包及项目目录发现 hooks.json，并只运行获准且启用的命令钩子。主要功能包括按指纹审阅和信任钩子、匹配工具名称、在模型上下文中附加钩子结果、通过设置页或 /hooks 管理，以及查看每回合运行统计。适合希望在 DSH 工作流中配置自动化检查、上下文补充或审批处理的用户；需要 Node.js 20+ 和 DSH，配置可放在 ~/.dsh/hooks.json。

dsh-codex-hooks adds lifecycle command hooks to DSH. It finds hooks.json in user, plugin, and project folders, then runs approved hooks on agent, tool, approval, and session events. Manage hooks in Settings or /hooks, match tools, add context, and view per-turn statistics. Requires Node.js 20+.
dsh-codex-hooks 的功能「多来源发现」：按当前用户配置、已安装插件包和已记住的项目目录查找 hooks.json，并在管理界面按来源分组。项目目录随会话工作区记录。
dsh-codex-hooks 的功能「事件钩子执行」：在 agent、工具调用、审批和会话生命周期事件触发配置的命令钩子；支持工具匹配、超时及把结果中的额外上下文带回模型流程。
dsh-codex-hooks 的功能「钩子审阅与管理」：在设置页查看待审阅钩子并进行信任、撤销或启停操作，也可用 /hooks 浏览钩子；信任状态绑定到当前钩子指纹。
dsh-codex-hooks 的功能「运行统计」：记录钩子执行状态，并在消息操作区查看对应回合的运行数、阻止数、失败数和历史；统计保存在当前进程的内存日志中。
dsh-codex-hooks 目前只实际执行 command 类型处理器；mcp_tool、prompt 和 agent 类型虽可被解析和审阅，但不会被派发执行。

怎样在工具调用前后接入自己的自动化钩子？
我希望按工具名称筛选哪些钩子会触发。
能不能让钩子结果补充给模型作为上下文？
想在 DSH 的审批请求时用规则自动允许或拒绝。
我需要一个界面来审阅和启用生命周期钩子。
I want to run custom commands at DSH agent and tool lifecycle events.
Can I review hooks and manage their trust from the DSH interface?

dsh-codex-hooks README · dsh-codex-hooks：**Codex's hook management, ported to [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).**

Codex gives every hook a review step, a fingerprint you approve once, a settings page, a `/hooks` browser and a stats panel. dsh ships none of that: it exposes interception seams and nothing around them. This plugin ports that management layer over, so hooks on dsh are reviewed, trusted, switched off and inspected the same way they are in Codex.

dsh-codex-hooks README · dsh-codex-hooks：The config file is dsh's own (`hooks.json` with dsh event names) — what is ported is the behaviour around it, not Codex's file format.

中文文档：[README.zh.md](README.zh.md)

dsh-codex-hooks README · Screenshots：Per-run detail lives behind the message action row. The **Hook stats** dialog reads one turn, names it, and lists that turn's runs with the session totals underneath — no turn picker, it answers for the message you opened it from. Every run belongs to the turn that triggered it, the way Codex binds a run to its turn id: the match is exact, and a turn the log never saw — including one numbered before a host restart — answers with `0` and a note, never with another turn's numbers. A read always resolves inside the session the user is working in — another session's same-numbered turn never stands in. The turn comes from the message: a message that ends a turn names it exactly, and a message of the turn that is running now answers for that turn:
dsh-codex-hooks README · Screenshots：The screenshots come from a local dsh install running the two `echo-hook` entries in `~/.dsh/hooks.json` — the same config the examples in this repo use.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Compatibility：| Plugin | Verified against |
| --- | --- |
| 0.5.x | dsh `0.1.0-rc.6` (development and self-test host, web + desktop) |

Newer dsh releases are untested: the plugin reads dsh's slot, command and remote-method contracts, and a host that renames one of those breaks it until it is updated.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Compatibility：The client half binds to four dsh client packages — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-commands` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat`. The first three ship with the profile; `dsh-client-ui-chat` is what provides the `conversation.chat.turnTail` slot the "open the stats of the message you clicked" feature needs, and on some installs it only exists inside the app's own `node_modules`. If the message-level hook button shows no turn, that package was the missing piece.

dsh-codex-hooks README · What it actually does：- **Discovers** `hooks.json` from three places, grouped in the UI:
  - **From Config** — `$DSH_HOME/hooks.json` (default `~/.dsh/hooks.json`).
  - **From Plugins** — every package inside the active profile that ships a `hooks.json`.
  - **From Projects** — `<workspace>/.dsh/hooks.json` for the workspaces this session has touched (up to 32 remembered).
- **Fingerprints** each hook: normalized JSON of the hook definition, `sha256:` over its UTF-8 bytes. The fingerprint is what the trust decision is pinned to, so editing a hook's command invalidates its trust instead of silently running new code.
- **Reviews trust per hook** in the settings page: new hooks start in *needs review*; you approve the current fingerprint, and the state lives in `$DSH_HOME/hooks.state.json` together with an independent enabled/disabled switch per hook.
- **Runs** `command` handlers only when they are enabled *and* trusted, with the hook's own timeout, `cwd`, environment and `command`/`commandWindows` split. Synchronous hooks for the same event start concurrently, matching Codex; results and additional context keep configuration order. An `approval/request` hook

dsh-codex-hooks README · Events：| Event | Fires | Can block |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent/pre-step` | a prompt was submitted, before the step runs | yes |
| `agent/request` | before the model request is sent | no |
| `tools/pre-execute` | before a tool call runs | yes |
| `tools/post-execute` | after a tool call finished | yes |
| `approval/request` | before a tool call asks for permission | yes |
| `agent/created` | a session starts | no |
| `agent/turn-stopping` | right before the turn ends | no |
| `session/disposed` | the session is disposed | no |
dsh-codex-hooks README · Events：Default timeout is 600s, except `session/disposed` (1s default, 3s maximum) so shutdown cannot hang.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Review, run history and `/hooks`：- **Hook button in the composer** — a hook icon sits in the composer's tool row (next to the permission and agent controls), with a small red dot while hooks still need review (no number — a count goes stale as soon as a hook is trusted elsewhere); clicking it opens the **Review hooks** dialog: one row per hook with a checkbox, the hook name, a *New* badge and a chevron that expands *Source / Hook type / Command / Timeout*, then the hint "You can change this later in Settings, under Hooks" (plain text: dsh exposes no API for a plugin to open a settings section, so it does not pretend to jump) and the three choices *Not now / Allow all / Allow selected*. Approving pins the current fingerprints in `$DSH_HOME/hooks.state.json`; everything else is handled later in **Settings → Hooks**, one hook at a time.
- **`/hooks` opens the hooks browser** — the first page lists the events with `active/installed` and a `!` marker on the events that need review, the second page lists the handlers of one event with their trust state, an on/off switch and a *Trust* / *Revoke* button. It is a normal dsh slash command (registered when the host co

dsh-codex-hooks README · Auto-approving a tool call：The hook prints `{"decision":"allow"}` to approve that one call, `{"decision":"deny","reason":"…"}`
to refuse it, or nothing at all to let the normal prompt ask. A deny from any hook wins over an
allow from another. `examples/approval-allow.mjs` only allows the tool named in
`APPROVAL_ALLOW_TOOL`, because a hook that approves everything silently removes the prompt.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Install：Requires dsh `0.1.0-rc.6` or newer and Node 20+.

```bash
dsh-codex-hooks README · from GitHub：dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:matata2017/dsh-codex-hooks

dsh-codex-hooks README · or from a local checkout, which is how this project is developed：dsh plugin --profile desktop add /path/to/dsh-codex-hooks
```

Restart the dsh web/desktop host afterwards, then open **Settings → Hooks**.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Configure：`~/.dsh/hooks.json`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "description": "my hooks",
  "hooks": {

One object per hook: `command` (or `type: "mcp_tool"` with `server` + `tool`), optional `matcher`, `timeout`, `statusMessage`, `additionalContextLimit`, `async`, `firstStepOnly`.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Configure：`firstStepOnly` (`agent/pre-step` only): `agent/pre-step` fires before **every step** of a turn. With `true`, the hook runs on the first step only (the one carrying the user message); later steps never start the command, and the stats dialog counts one run per turn. Use it for hooks that only care about the prompt (memory recall, prompt rewriting). It is part of the trust fingerprint, so adding it asks for review again; leaving it out or `false` keeps the fingerprint unchanged.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Configure：Handler types: `command` is the only one executed. `mcp_tool`, `prompt` and `agent` are parsed and reviewable but not dispatched — they show up as installed, never as active, because a hook that silently does nothing is worse than one that says so.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Verification status：- `node test/run-tests.mjs` → **99 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.
- `node selftest/host-e2e.mjs` → **20 passed, 0 failed** against a real profile.
- `agent/pre-step` runs in a live dsh session once the hook is trusted: the example hook prints one `echo-hook received event=…` line per agent step (it fires before every step, so one prompt can produce several lines). A hook stays untrusted until you approve it in the review dialog or in Settings → Hooks; an untrusted hook never runs.
dsh-codex-hooks README · What a hook cannot do here：These are dsh boundaries, not missing code: they need a seam the harness does not expose. Codex has these; dsh does not, so the port stops here.
section: What a hook cannot do here

text:
dsh-codex-hooks README · What a hook cannot do here：- **Context is user-role only.** `agent/pre-step` takes `UserMessage[]`, and no public API appends a developer message, so `additionalContext` cannot arrive with the extra weight a developer message would carry.
- **Tool arguments cannot be rewritten.** `tools/pre-execute` returns allow / deny / ask / cancel; dsh deliberately excludes input rewriting because arguments are already logged and presented.
- **No seam for compaction, interrupt, or model-request events.** `agent/created` with `source: "compact"` is the closest thing to a post-compaction hook.
- **`mcp_tool`, `prompt`, `agent` handlers are reviewable but not executed**, so they never show as active.
section: What a hook cannot do here

text: dsh-codex-hooks README · Security：Hooks execute real commands with the permissions of the dsh process. That is why trust is pinned to the sha256 fingerprint of each hook: approving a hook approves exactly that command line, and any edit requires a new approval. Only enable hooks you have read.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Security：Approval sticks. The trust state is written to a temporary file and renamed over the real one, so an interrupted write can never leave a half-file that the next read would reject — and a click that would land on the button that just replaced it is ignored, so granting trust cannot revoke it again a moment later.

dsh-codex-hooks README · Client bundles share one global scope：The browser loader concatenates every installed plugin client bundle into a single script, so a top-level `const` is visible to all plugins. Two plugins that pick the same name is a `SyntaxError` that stops the whole app from booting, not just one plugin. This client bundle therefore runs inside its own function and declares nothing globally.
section: Client bundles share one global scope
